extensionDescription.message: Search selected text with up to 5 preconfigured options. Use the context menu on desktop, or the popup panel shown on text selection in environments without contextMenus support (e.g. Firefox for Android / Iceraven).

optionsDescription.message:
You can register up to 5 search options to show in the context menu.
The search engine can be chosen per option, and the prefix is a string prepended to the selected text when searching (e.g. site:stackoverflow.com).
The settings here are reflected identically in the context menu on desktop and in the popup panel shown on text selection in environments without contextMenus support (e.g. Firefox for Android / Iceraven).

customEnginesDescription.message: You can add your own search engines. Enter a name and a search URL containing %s where the query should be inserted (e.g. https://example.com/search?q=%s).

operatorsDescription.message: Search operators are keywords that refine a query. Combine them in the prefix field to search like an expert.

opExcludeEffect.message: Pages that do not contain the excluded word

opSiteEffect.message: Check the indexed pages of a domain

opSiteKeywordEffect.message: Search only within a specific site

opIntitleEffect.message: Pages with the word in the title

opAllintitleEffect.message: Pages with all words in the title

opInurlEffect.message: Pages with the string in the URL

opIntextEffect.message: Pages with the word in the body

operatorsFileNote.message: Especially useful when looking for reliable primary sources.

opAfterEffect.message: On or after the specified date

opBeforeEffect.message: On or before the specified date

opTipBroad.message: Start broad, then narrow down while checking the results.

opTipExclude.message: Use exclusion (-) to remove noise such as unrelated fields with the same name.

opTipPrimary.message: Combine site: and filetype: to jump straight to primary sources.

opTipEnglish.message: Searching in English often changes the amount of information significantly.

operatorsNote.message: Google may not strictly process operators these days. If results differ from your expectations, adjust by adding quotes or reducing words. Many operators also work on Bing, DuckDuckGo and others, but the details differ.
